hook.line: Don Hernando never hides what he thinks. When Tomás left the meeting early without a word, Hernando told him exactly how it struck him, and Spanish has a frame for that.
hook.es: Me pareció muy mal que te fueras sin despedirte.
hook.en: I thought it was really wrong of you to leave without saying goodbye.

examples.es: Me pareció muy mal que te fueras sin despedirte.
examples.en: I thought it was really wrong of you to leave without saying goodbye.

examples.es: Me pareció muy bien que le dijeras la verdad.
examples.en: I thought it was very good that you told him the truth.

examples.es: Me pareció pésimo que no nos avisaran.
examples.en: I thought it was terrible that they didn't let us know.

examples.es: A Hernando le pareció mal que Tomás llegara tarde.
examples.en: Hernando thought it was wrong that Tomás arrived late.

examples.es: Nos pareció genial que Vale hiciera el pastel.

examples.es: Me cayó muy mal que no me llamaran.
examples.en: It really bothered me that they didn't call me.

rule:
To say how someone's action struck you, use *me pareció* + a judgement + *que* + a verb in the *-ra* form: *Me pareció muy mal que te fueras*.

Judgements: *bien, mal, pésimo, genial, increíble*, with *muy* if you like. Who judges: *me, te, le, nos, les*.

The *-ra* verbs (*fueras, dijeras, avisaran*) follow because the judgement is in the past. English says "that you left"; Spanish uses the subjunctive, never the plain past. *Me cayó mal que…* is the same idea with more feeling.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the past subjunctive after expressions of evaluation.

readAndPick.es: Me pareció muy mal que te fueras.
options: I thought it was very good that you left.
I thought it was very wrong that you left.
I think you'll leave.

readAndPick.es: Me pareció muy bien que le dijeras la verdad.
options: I thought it was very bad that you told him.
I was told the truth.
I thought it was very good that you told him the truth.

readAndPick.es: Me pareció pésimo que no nos avisaran.
options: I thought it was terrible that they didn't let us know.
I thought it was great that they let us know.
I thought it was terrible that you didn't tell them.

readAndPick.es: A Hernando le pareció mal que Tomás llegara tarde.
options: Tomás thought it was wrong that Hernando arrived late.
Hernando thought it was wrong that Tomás arrived late.
Hernando thought it was fine that Tomás arrived late.

readAndPick.es: Nos pareció genial que Vale hiciera el pastel.
options: I thought it was great that Vale made the cake.
We thought it was awful that Vale made the cake.
We thought it was great that Vale made the cake.

readAndPick.es: Me cayó muy mal que no me llamaran.
options: It really pleased me that they called me.
It really bothered me that they didn't call me.
It bothered them that I didn't call.
Do you think it's fine that we close early?
Did you think it was wrong that we closed early?
Did you think it was fine that we closed early?

readAndPick.es: Me parece mal que te vayas.
options: I think it's wrong that you're leaving.
I thought it was wrong that you left.
I think it's wrong that I'm leaving.

yourTurn.prompt: I thought it was very wrong of you (*tú*) to leave. Fill the gap: Me pareció muy mal que ___. (*te fuiste* or *te fueras*)
yourTurn.answer: Me pareció muy mal que te fueras.
yourTurn.why: After *me pareció mal que*, use the *-ra* form.

yourTurn.prompt: I thought it was very good that you (*tú*) told him the truth.
yourTurn.answer: Me pareció muy bien que le dijeras la verdad.
yourTurn.why: *Dijeras* is the *tú* form of the *-ra* verb.

yourTurn.prompt: I thought it was terrible that they didn't let us know.
yourTurn.answer: Me pareció pésimo que no nos avisaran.
yourTurn.why: *Pésimo* is the strongest judgement, and *avisaran* is the *-ra* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Hernando thought it was wrong that Tomás arrived late.
yourTurn.answer: A Hernando le pareció mal que Tomás llegara tarde.
accept: Le pareció mal a Hernando que Tomás llegara tarde.
yourTurn.why: *Le* stands for Hernando, and *llegara* is the *-ra* form.

yourTurn.prompt: We thought it was great that Vale made the cake.
yourTurn.answer: Nos pareció genial que Vale hiciera el pastel.
yourTurn.why: *Nos* says we are the ones judging.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend (*tú*): did you think it was fine that we closed early?
yourTurn.why: The same frame works as a question, with *te* for the friend.

yourTurn.prompt: It really bothered me that they didn't call me.
yourTurn.answer: Me cayó muy mal que no me llamaran.
yourTurn.why: *Me cayó mal que* is the stronger, more personal version.

pitfalls.wrong: Me pareció mal que te fuiste.
pitfalls.right: Me pareció mal que te fueras.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After a judgement like this, Spanish uses the *-ra* form, not the plain past.

pitfalls.wrong: Me pareció mal de que te fueras.
pitfalls.right: Me pareció mal que te fueras.

pitfalls.wrong: Me parece mal que te fueras ayer.
pitfalls.right: Me pareció mal que te fueras ayer.
pitfalls.why: The judgement is about the past, so *pareció* matches *fueras*.

personal: Think of something a friend did. Say how it struck you. Start with *Me pareció…*
